reviews.name: Millicent Hunter
reviews.text:
I am very disappointed in the treatment I received at Woodminster Vet Hospital.  I had taken my young puppy to them since I picked her up from the breeder in 2025.   Initially all was good however on 3 separate occasions when I received a receipt with my pets name on the first page and a list of vaccinations she received during the visit.  I noted that on the second page in black and white were written instructions for another dog who had sustained an insect bite.  When I contacted the office the first and second times this occurred I was assured that they would take care of removing this false documentation from my pets medical record.   On the third time I noted the same language, I insisted on speaking to the manager and owner to voice my concerns which I had to place in writing two times to actually get it done because they stated  it was just the receipt and that my pets medical record was accurate .   As a health care professional with 46+ years of experience I am concerned about their lack of knowledge and understanding that any and all medical record documentation needs to be accurate.  After finally getting the paperwork amended and talking to the owner who profusely apologized,  I thought everything was resolved. Unfortunately, when I called to make a follow up appointment for my pets routine vaccination on 6/26/26 I was first told they didn’t have any available appointments which was untrue because my friend who I recently referred to them made an appointment on the same day.  After thinking about it I called back and was then told that I needed to talk to the coordinator before I could book an appointment and she wasn’t in the office and would call me back sometime the following week.   Of note it is now Tuesday 6/30/26 and the office manager has not called me nor sent an email.

It is now obvious to me that I was banned from the office for making a complaint about a mistake thier office made and no one had the dignity or respect to call me or send a letter so that I can find a new vet for my pet.

I would not recommend going here as I feel their lack of  integrity and tack which is a big ticket item for me when dealing with anyone who provides care to animals and people, especially when the cost of care is not cheap nor free.

reviews.text: Nice that they offer a free exam to shelter adoptees, however I got a really weird vibe here and will not be going back. They took my kittens into the back and told me to wait in an exam room and the doctor/kittens would be in shortly. I waited in there an hour. It may be policy to separate you from your pets at some vets, but it was very off putting for me. I gave no permission to do any sort of service without consulting me first, so what were they doing back there? Why the wait? A vet tech and eventually doctor came into the exam room, but they did not bring the kittens. I had wanted the doctor to make sure their spay sites were healing ok, but she was very vague and I am not sure she even looked at them. How would I know? They were in the back the whole time. reviews.name: Gaines
reviews.text:
Something feels VERY WRONG here. Our first time there, we are double charged for $200+ blood test fee. When we called to have the money refunded, we had to choose between keeping it on account or having a check mailed to us. We chose check but had to call several more times over several weeks to actually get it.

In regards to the blood test that I mentioned. After a week, we called to find out if they had the results yet and they did. The person we spoke with felt very rude and dismissive. They told us the doctor would call us when they had time. we asked  when the tests had been ready and they refused to tell us and wouldn't provide us a copy of the tests. It took over another week for the doctor to call us with the results of our blood test that they apparently perform in-house.

Then we go to get our meds refilled for the first time since they were filled at our last vet, and the cost here was almost $90 when at the last vet, it was less than $20. I asked for a written prescription so that I could goto a pharmacy where it would only cost $10-20 and they told me that our vet was on vacation for 2 weeks so they could not write me a prescription and if I wanted to see one of their other veterinarians I could book and pay $60 for the appointment.

So I must say CLIENT BEWARE AND STEER CLEAR. This isn't just a one-off experience with them. This is multiple interactions over multiple months. Something is not right here. It just feels off.

I urge you to read between the lines of the good reviews and pay attention to the experience of the bad reviewers. There seems to be an identifiable trend of overcharging and unethical practices.

reviews.name: Stacy Star
reviews.text: BEWARE!!!  Rip off. I took my 4 year old dog in for an ear infection. This is the second time she had one so I already knew what it was. I paid $25 holding deposit and the exam was a total of $65. The assistant asked if they can put a muzzle on her and I said that was fine. Later the assistant comes back and tells me I have to pay $500 in order to sedate her because she would not sit still. I refused because my dog has never needed to be sedated anywhere else. They told me I can take my dog back to her original vet and I was more than happy to do so. I took my dog the next day to PetVet which is a wonderful place where I Was able to look at them while giving her the exam. They also cleaned her ears and put the medicine in both ears without a fight. My dog was super calm. They wanted to rip me off $500 in order for them to look in both of her ears.

After again I asked them if they require the blood test they told me they no longer want me as a patient because of communication issues and pushed me to see another vet for the procedure. Seems like the miscommunication was the money talk they see in patients and if they don't get what they want they push you to another vet. Wasted a 2 hour commute across the bridge to deal with this. reviews.name: Julian Fountain
reviews.text: After setting up an appointment online, I brought our 11 y/o cat in as a new patient to Woodminster because she had a significant infection and swelling.  While many vets are not taking new patients due to COVID, Woodminster agreed to fit her in within a few hours of my calling.  They did a good job with all COVID precautions.  The cat is not one to participate in anything that isn't her idea, but they were very kind and diplomatic in discussing her temperament and dealing with her.  They were able to treat the infection, made good suggestions for diagnostics, provided good instructions for home care, followed up with test results and to inquire about her progress, and the cat is now in her usual state of good health 2 weeks later.  They provided excellent care and excellent customer service.

reviews.name: Lj Roberts
reviews.text:

I appreciated that our wait time for someone to take him in was relatively short.  I appreciated the honesty of the doctor. reviews.name: Neshi bae
reviews.text: I know you can’t put a price on the love you have for you companion (dog, cat, etc) However there is a huge difference between paying what’s a fare price and being swindled! I rescued a dog a few weeks ago,  I found her alone under a dumpster. I didn’t have any information and history on her. I tried clipping her nails on my own, because I got her in the beginning of the pandemic and most grooming places were still closed. I got most of them but unfortunately there was one I couldn’t get to. After about a week or so they nail became ingrown. I figured it would be best to take her to a vet. I called Woodminster and I got a quote over the phone. They quoted me the most I would pay would be $250 (this was supposed to include $55 visit, $25 to cut the nails, $40-90 for sedation, and $17 rabies shot and maybe $40 for antibiotics) when we showed up for our appointment we waited over half an hour for one of the assistance to come get our girl. She was in the back for about 30 minutes when the assistant showed up with an estimate ledger quoting $807.06!!!! My Goodness!!!! $807.06 to remove an ingrown nail! Now they wanted to charge me this because they insisted on putting her to sleep to do the procedure. They said my dog wasn’t easy to work with, my 15 lb dog wasn’t being nice. To sedation was $155.63 and they up the price to cut the nail to $175.00!!!! We went from $25 to cut the nail to $175! After talking to the assistant about the price we were quoted and letting her hear the voicemail that was left my Reina two days before she said she would talk to the veterinarian about doing it for that price. She didn’t agree to do it, since we already had to pay $55 for the visit we decided to get some shots that she needed! They gave me a receipt for the visits but didn’t want to provide immunization records. What?! How?! So I pressed for them to give me the immunization records. Finally after waiting 30 more minutes they finally gave me the records. I asked for a prescription for a sedative to help my dog, but both of the veterinarians on shift refused to give one to me saying that they didn’t feel comfortable! Oh but you feel comfortable charging me $807 to cut a nail?! I feel lied and lured to come here with fake quotes and estimates. I do not believe in my heart that anyone on shift that day truly cares for the well being of my pup! After being at Woodminster for over 3 1/2 hours, I left with a $100 less and a pup that still needed help! I found a dog groomer, who charged me $5 and Took care of the nail in less than two minutes. It saddens me that something that could’ve been done in two minutes was dangled over my head and was gonna cost me $807. The veterinarian on shift was Dr Adar and Dr Salwan. I am going to move forward on contact the veterinarian board.  This establishment needs to be looked into. Moral of the story don’t bring your companions here, these people have no compassion for animals!!!!! None!!!!

No smile, no hand shake, no warmth whatsoever.  After talking to the vet for about 8 minutes, and asking only one real question about what flea medicine I should use, the vet stepped out and said she's give us some info on that. I bought the flea meds which I checked later to be about $40 more than what I could buy them for anywhere else. I'll stick with my regular vet who is not only superb at his job, but warm and genuine, the kind of person that acknowledged my child's existence and even took us back to his office once to teach him about x-rays. reviews.text:
Avoid at all costs - extremely incompetent and as other reviews mention, they do not care about your animals in the same way other vets do based on my experience.  I came in to have my dog checked out for excessive scratching (she had scratched a patch of fur off of her back). They asked to do a skin test on the area that was scratched and indicated it would be 30m. Came back in 30m and they told me she's still not ready - "it will only be another 30m." 30m later, still not ready! Finally after almost 2 hours, she was ready to be picked up. I asked about the results of the test and if it could be allergies, and I got a blank stare from the nurse. Eventually, I got a bogus response that didn't even answer my question. Overall, it was a horrible experience at the vet during my visit. But here's an example of the true incompetence of this place:

I called back recently to have an airline form filled out by the vet, indicating my dog was checked out by the vet (the vet filled out almost the exact same form for me the day of our exam for a different airline). Initially, they told me it would be "no problem" and to "just send the form via email and they'll have it filled out and sent back ASAP." After 5 emails, and almost daily calls for 2 weeks, I was told THE DAY BEFORE I NEEDED THE FORM, that they couldn't fill it out ...the dog needed to be examined within 10 days in order to complete the form. This would have been great to know initially instead of continuing to tell me they would have it filled out and get it back to me. Day after day of calling, I kept getting the same answer - "we're working on it and will get it to you." Now it's too late and my dog will not be able to travel with me. Complete incompetence from the entire staff at Woodminster. If I could give zero stars I absolutely would. Avoid this place -- plenty of better vets out there.

reviews.name: Lisa Howe
reviews.text:
I have given Woodminster Veterinary almost a month to provide some type of closure for our horrible experience. My family has not  received call back in some time so it is with a heavy hear that I write this review.

We brought our beloved cat into Woodminster Vet 4 months ago for a checkup and we were looking for a Veterinarian closer to our home. Several tests were recommended in addition to a deep teeth cleaning. We trusted the recommendations and went ahead with the procedure. Unfortunately our cat never recovered from the anesthesia and had to be put to sleep. We were devastated to say the least but the events that occurred during his last two days were a nightmare.

1. I was charged for flea medication and antibiotics prior to the procedure which totaled around 250$. The day my husband picked up our cat from the dental cleaning he was charged for the exact same thing that I had just paid for. We did not realize until the next day that had happened.

2. I knew immediately that something was wrong when i picked up our cat. I took him home and hours later called the clinic. Labs were recommended to explore the issue. I asked what the labs could show and what they were looking for and was yelled at and berated by Dr. Adar. She refused to answer my questions and yelled "because I am the Dr". When i brought our cat back in that afternoon she continued to yell and humiliate me for questioning the labs. I left in tears confused and not knowing what to do. I eventually returned after our cat would not eat for 4 days and he was sadly put down.

3. I contacted Woodminster a week after this experience to express my disappointment. I felt taken advantage of in a time of need, hurt, embarrassed and angry that this procedure which ultimately killed my cat was even recommended. I spoke with the office manager Hannah who assured me she would make some resolution. She reported that she was there while the Dr. screamed at me and that she was so sorry I had to go through this. She apologized profusely for Dr. Adar's behavior and the unethical double charge for medications. She promised she would talk with the supervisor and contact me back. I waited an entire week before calling back. She again said she would get back to me asap- another week and nothing! I finally received a call saying they would refund me 95$ (the procedure, labs, medications and putting our cat to sleep cost over 1,000$!!!!!). I never received a call from the supervisor and in addition never even received  the 95$.

I want to caution other pet owners from taking their animals to Woodminster Vet . Please click on the "Unsubstantiated Reviews (I.E. the reviews they pay to block) and see others horrible experiences. We can never get our cat back but i am hoping reading this will save another family the hardship we have endured.

reviews.name: Jamie L

reviews.name: Kevin Brinkley
reviews.text: Last year my 16-year-old cat Sassafras died suddenly on a Sunday.  Woodminster Veterinarian Hospital was the only vet clinic around that was open at the time.  They treated us with such care, kindness and compassion that I plan to be a loyal customer as long as I'm in the Bay Area.  I now have two young and feisty cats who go to Woodminster for all of their check-ups.  The Woodminster vets never try to up-sell us on unnecessary procedures.  I have complete trust in their recommendations.  I've had many negative experiences with other Bay Area vets, so it's a relief to find a clinic staffed with caring and trustworthy experts.  I'd recommend this clinic to anyone in the Bay Area, even if they have to have to drive a little farther, like I do.

reviews.name: Jeremy Laurin
reviews.text: Great veterinarians here! They are so good to my little dog and very flexible when anything has come up. I highly recommend them!

reviews.name: Shobhana Alice Schwebke
reviews.text: I love this place! I took my little dog for a tooth extraction.  She has a problem letting anyone touch her teeth, so she has to have anesthesia to even clean her teeth.  I had been able to brush her teeth, but somehow she chipped a back tooth so she needed anesthesia for the extraction. Everyone was so friendly and helpful. And what I like best is they ALL took the time to explain everything to me, not just the procedure, but the billing and the recovery.  I was sent home with complete instructions on her recovery.  The clinic feels like a community and I also appreciate their informative newsletters.

reviews.name: Claire Svitek
reviews.text:
So very close by. Such a caring & knowledgeable staff and veterinarians always willing to go the extra mile and willing to take the time to explain and re-explain if need-be things to you . PLUS it is such a very comfortable place to take your pet since it's located at the back of a little trafficked loop street to take your pet for a pleasant walk before or after their appointment..The quiet location is a huge plus for me, as when I'm taking my pup to the Vet she's already stressed (and so am I! smile) if she's not feeling well or is just going to get her annual shots(she seems to know when). It so nice to not have to look for parking and then not to have to get out of my car onto a busy street. Their hours are great and their prices seem to be competitive as well.

You can grab a burger(the best you'll ever find!) at Woodminster Cafe. AND there is a hardware store directly across the street too!; you can run off to for all the things you've forgotten to get when at Home Depot!

This is all you have to remember to find this quiet stress free location:
Simply enter from Mountain Blvd, just remember to enter from the correct end of the loop going between the Round Table Pizza on one side and the little market on the opposite side of the street(at this point it is 2 way but when you go to exit on other side of loop you are heading the correct way when it become 1 way). The office is on the left & parking lot is on right a little ahead.

reviews.name: Serena Jones
reviews.text:
I am so grateful to Woodminster Veterinary Hospital for their excellent care for my formerly feral cat. I took him to another vet in an emergency (that was open midnight) and they said he would die without a risky thousand dollar transfusion and maybe even then. They wouldn't consider any other treatment for his blood parasite. Not even palliative care.
When he survived the night, the next day the vet at Woodminster said we could try something else and worked out a treatment where they cared for him during the day with IVs when I was working and I took him home every night.  Three days later the parasite was dead and my cat was alive and better. And for far less than the risky transfusion. I appreciated her cleverness and willingness to think outside the box. And I love my cat but money and taking time off work were issues for me as they are for many of us. I also appreciated that they did not make me feel like a bad owner for considering cost when choosing treatment.  My cat and I are living happily ever after.

reviews.name: J Brooks
reviews.text:
So far this has been the only vet clinic I've been to where the staff seemed to genuinely care about my dogs. We dealt with a tricky skin condition for one of my dogs and while it did involve a lot of trial and error, I could tell the staff really wanted my dog to be healthy and comfortable. On top of that, nearly everyone there has been super friendly and very supportive. Dr. Odar really listens, does her research,  and her calm demeanor is ideal for nervous pets (and pet owners!). I've already recommended this place to a few friends.

I have to say the biggest downside is the parking situation. It's a tiny neighborhood with 2 or 3 spots designated for the vet clinic, and most of the street parking has meters. God forbid you park for a half hour at the salon across the street-- emergency or not they WILL try to tow your car :/

Anyway, my general experience here has been a very positive one.

reviews.name: Tara
reviews.text:
my experience from 2013-I planned to NOT review woodminster after poor experience a few years ago, but since I just received an email asking me to rate them on yelp unless its bad, and then could I just tell them directly instead of rating them on yelp, I decided enough was enough.
Most important, the veterinary care was fine. I did wait two hours with my cat in the lobby past time of appointment, had to go to work, and left him longer so staff could clean his ears. returned to a big bill, no ears cleaned, had to call back rework bill. had other experiences similarly.
No one could identify the bright red larvae of the harvest mite/chigger poking out of my cat's hide that was causing puss and irritation. Additionally I believed my cats had ear mites which the vets disagreed with. My boy cat had a terrible ear infection and was very sick, you could hear the fluid inside when he shook his head, so he was treated with ear drops that kind of helped. The staff was untimely with callbacks and prescriptions, I had to cb many times to get directions on the prescription, it was pretty annoying. My cat didnt really get better either, until i used zymox, which is an over the counter steroid drop that supposedly has helpful enymes in it, and I found that online.  Back to the earmites-I'm certain ear mites caused a reaction in my maine coon boy cat's ear to start infection, bc my other cats had earmites and were scratchy (new woodsy home w/ lots of wild critters). He always reacts differently to allergens than my other short hair tabbies, and his brown ear goo wasnt as bad but it was still ear goo. I researched and found ivermectin applied to cats for earmites is common in catteries, and i asked vet about new products containing ivermectin but since not fda approved unable to prescribe. You can use revolution every three weeks to break the ear mite cycle as well. I ended up buying ivermectin from jeffers livestock and applying 3ccs to each cat to control ear mites. ivermectin is a parasite/wormer and kills various invertebrates that have no blood brain barrier thus worms, mites, but not fleas. so hopefully it was killing tapeworm but I dont know. That's why I see a vet, so i can do research and he can tell me if I'm being stupid, but that's the primary skill of a vet besides medicine, COMMUNICATION and FOLLOW UP. otherwise your business is a disaster.
Anyways, I believe the vets are caring about animals and competent, the front desk staff was sugar sweet, there were logistically a nightmare to deal with, but maybe that's changed.

What they do care about is competent and kind care, and Woodminster's vets and staff provide that in spades.  They're great - and are the vet of choice for our beloved little rescue dog Gus!

reviews.name: nancy meginness
reviews.text: Excellent care for my dog, competitive pricing, great office hours and friendly staff make this the place to take any pet.  My 6 year old pom-chi has been going there for about 7 months now. The entire staff is welcoming, well informed and I have every confidence in the medical care she is getting there.  I had to bring her in for an emergency visit recently and was able to get in that same day with a procedure conducted the following day.  Further, when she had an allergic reaction to her rabies shot at 6:00 p.m. one evening, I was able to take her right in for treatment.  My old vet clinic would have sent me to the animal emergency hospital at that time of day, which would have cost a fortune. The care here is wonderful and the prices are quite reasonable. As mentioned above, you can't beat their hours either.

reviews.name: Jenny Kao
reviews.text: The staff at Woodminster, from the front desk staff to the vets, are top-notch and superb. Their prices are lower than other nearby vet hospitals but their service is comparable. I also happen to have a cat that is scared to death of riding in cars, so the vet at Woodminster was nice enough to call me with the name and number of a mobile vet, rather than trying to convince me to bring him back in to Woodminster. Please give them a try -- they are a wonderful group of animal lovers who are also very respectful of and sensitive to the needs of pet owners.
